newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps - fuel, mogas gain, others steady.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps - fuel, mogas gain, others steady.

text.p: European oil swaps were easier on Friday bar stronger high sulphur fuel and gasoline swaps.
Brent CFDs were broadly steady, losing a couple of cents, while low sulphur fuel came under heavier pressure.
Traders said Brent CFDs dipped with June 2-6 down to -32 cents under July from 30/31 cents with further out weeks following a similar pattern.
A dated Brent traded at a weaker July Brent -30 cents today for June 12-14 dates compared with Thursday's July -24 cents.

Gasoline gained about $2 a tonne to around $207 for June, backed by tightness in the Mediterranean and marginally bullish APIs which showed a draw earlier in the week. Further out levels were dragged higher by June values, but retained a steady $5.75-$6 backwardation.
Traders said the near-term outlook was looking more bullish with a stronger possibility of material heading transatlantic.
High sulphur fuel oil showed a 50 cent to $1 rise with June traded at $83.25, $83.50 and $83.75. Physical barges traded in the morning at $82 and $82.50 before edging up to $83.50.
The cloud of Russian material was hanging over the ARA market, but some support came from fairly good demand for high sulphur fuel outside of NWE.

Low sulphur fuel swaps were pulled down $2 or so as a couple of physical cargoes weighed on a quiet market. Traders said June was pegged around $93 with July $1 in contango. The prospect of NWE material heading to the U.S has pressured swaps, traders said.
EN590 diesel swaps came under more pressure having slipped steadily since last week. June was heard offered at $8 over the IPE gas oil.
Naphtha swaps were steady in a sloppy market, showing a very minimal drop of 25 cents or so with June pegged at $188 and July at $188.50.
